field_triage.name: Field triage (2021)
field_triage.source: Newgard CD et al. National Guideline for the Field Triage of Injured Patients: Recommendations of the National Expert Panel on Field Triage, 2021. J Trauma Acute Care Surg 2022;93(2):e49-e60
field_triage.thresholds: Red: transport to the highest-level trauma center; Yellow: preferentially a trauma center (need not be the highest level)

criteria.label: Unable to follow commands (motor GCS < 6)
RR < 10 or > 29
Room-air SpO2 < 90%
SBP below the age limit
SBP < 70 + 2×age (age 0-9)
SBP < 110 (age ≥ 65)
HR > SBP (age ≥ 10)
Anticoagulant use

gfast.name: G.F.A.S.T.
gfast.source: Santa Clara County EMS Protocol 700-A13 Stroke (effective 2026-01-01), sections 2.3 and 3.2-3.3
gfast.thresholds: 4 of 4 = Comprehensive Stroke Center (closest stroke center if > 45 min transport); 3 or fewer = closest stroke center (Policy 602)

news2.name: NEWS2
news2.source: Royal College of Physicians. National Early Warning Score (NEWS) 2: Standardising the assessment of acute-illness severity in the NHS. London: RCP; December 2017

race.name: RACE
race.source: Pérez de la Ossa N et al., Stroke 2014;45:87-91 (RACE scale)

sepsis_700a04.name: Sepsis pre-notification (700-A04)
sepsis_700a04.source: Santa Clara County EMS Protocol 700-A04 Sepsis (effective 2026-01-01; replaces 2025-01-01), §1.3-1.4, page 1 of 1
sepsis_700a04.thresholds: 700-A04 §1.4: "Advanced notification to hospital of suspected sepsis patient if two or more SIRS criteria are met"

criteria.label: 1.4. Advanced notification to hospital of suspected sepsis patient if two or more SIRS criteria are met
Suspected infection (700-A04 §1.4, §4.1)
1.3. Identification of Systemic Inflammatory Response Syndrome (SIRS) Criteria (two or more, §1.4)
1.3.1. Temperature less than 96 °F or greater than 100.4 °F
1.3.2. Heart rate greater than 90 bpm
1.3.3. Respiratory rate greater than 20 bpm
1.3.4. ETCO2 less than 25 mmHg

trauma_605.name: Trauma Alert criteria (Policy 605)
trauma_605.source: Santa Clara County EMS Policy 605 Prehospital Trauma Triage (effective 2025-04-01, in AO 2025-005), §II.B criteria A-X (policy pp. 1-3) and §III.A (p. 3); PDF pages 25-27 of AO 2025-005
trauma_605.thresholds: 605 §II.B: "Injured patients are to be identified as a Trauma Alert Patient if one or more of the criteria below are met" (Red or Yellow; Policy 602 §VI.C). Special considerations X are EMS judgement. Major burn criteria (§III) are shown separately.

groups.label: High Risk Injury Pattern / Mental Status and Vital Signs (Red Criteria)
Moderate Risk Mechanism of Injury (Yellow Criteria)
Special Considerations (EMS Judgement), §II.B X: "The following should be considered in prehospital trauma triage when a traumatic injury is also present"

criteria.label: A. Penetrating injuries to head, neck, torso, and proximal extremities
B. Skull deformity, suspected skull fracture
C. Suspected spinal injury with new motor or sensory loss
D. Chest wall instability, deformity, or suspected flail chest
E. Suspected pelvic fracture
F. Suspected fracture of two or more proximal long bones
G. Crushed, degloved, mangled, or pulseless extremity
H. Amputation proximal to wrist or ankle
I. Active bleeding requiring a tourniquet or wound packing with continuous pressure
Described: bleeding requiring tourniquet or wound packing
Procedure done: tourniquet or wound packing
J. Unable to follow commands (motor GCS <6)
K. Respiratory rate less than 10 or greater than 29 breaths per minute
L. Respiratory distress or need for respiratory support
Described: respiratory distress or need for respiratory support
Procedure done: BVM ventilation, CPAP, supraglottic airway or intubation
M. Room-air pulse oximetry less than 90%
N. Vital signs below the following parameters (systolic BP by age)
N.1 Age 0-9 years: Systolic BP less than 70 mmHg + 2x age years
N.2 Age 10-64 years: Systolic BP less than 90 mmHg
N.3 Age older than 65 years: Systolic BP is less than 110 mmHg
N.4 Age 10 and older: Heart rate is greater than Systolic BP
O. Auto crash with partial or complete ejection
P. Auto crash with intrusion > 12 inches occupant site, > 18 inches any site, or need for extrication
Q. Death in passenger compartment
R. Child (age 0-9) unrestrained or in unsecure child safety seat
Described: child unrestrained
Age 0-9
T. Rider separated from transport vehicle with significant impact (eg. Motorcycle, ATV, horse etc.)
U. Rollover with unrestrained occupant
V. Pedestrian/bicycle rider thrown, run over, or with significant impact
W. Fall from height > 10 feet (all ages)
X.1 Patients with minor traumatic injuries also on anti-coagulants or with bleeding disorders
X.2 Time-sensitive extremity injury
X.6 Low-level falls with significant head impact
X.7 Any pregnant patient beyond 20 weeks gestation (uterine fundus palpated at or above the umbilicus) in cardiac arrest, that does not meet obvious death criteria
Pregnant beyond 20 weeks
In cardiac arrest (CPR or defibrillation recorded)
III.A Patients with burn injuries are to be identified as major burn criteria (§III.A.1-7); §III.B "Transport all identified major burn patients to a designated burn center"
